dct_description_sm: Litter decomposition is a major factor influencing nutrient availability of soil in forest ecosystems. The decomposition rate of litter is affected by environmental factors such as temperature. We think that conifers can impoverish soils in cold climates by immobilising nutrients and, thereby, exclude more demanding deciduous species. In this study, we investigate the interplay of tree species, litter quality, decomposition, and nutrient availability on tree growth.  Soil nutrient concentrations and their supply were measured in sub-arctic black spruce (Picea mariana) and white birch (Betula papyrifera) stands and are compared with southern boreal forest sites.
dct_title_s: Vegetation and soil data in Schefferville area, Qubec
